tuning_strategies: Incorporation of 5 mol% BaZrO₃ nanoparticles into YBCO matrix via pulsed laser deposition using composite ceramic targets
tuning_effects: Induced 9.4% lattice mismatch between YBCO and BaZrO₃ particles, generating dense c-axis-aligned edge dislocations (<50 nm spacing) with density >400 μm⁻². Achieved 1.5-5× enhancement in Jc (75.5 K) across 1-7 T fields compared to pure YBCO, particularly showing 5× improvement at 7 T.

tuning_strategies: Generation of correlated linear defects through heteroepitaxial strain from BaZrO₃ nanoparticles
tuning_effects: Created columnar defect structures acting as strong pinning centers, demonstrated by angular Jc dependence showing enhanced c-axis peak (inset Fig.1a). Maintained Jc improvement across 0°-80° field orientations with Fp/Fpmax ratio increase from 0.3 (pure YBCO) to 0.45 (YBCO+BaZrO₃) at 4T.

tuning_strategies: Heteroepitaxial growth control using SrTiO₃ (STO)-buffered IBAD-MgO substrates
tuning_effects: Achieved cube-on-cube in-plane alignment between YBCO matrix and BaZrO₃ particles (φ-scan FWHM <2°), enabling effective strain transfer. Maintained high Jc (>0.1 MA/cm² at 4.5T) in practical conductors through optimized interfacial lattice matching.

tuning_strategies: Dual-axis texture propagation from IBAD-MgO substrates through STO buffer layer
tuning_effects: Enabled (00l)-oriented YBCO growth with BaZrO₃ (110)||YBCO (103) orientation relationship, confirmed by XRD pole figures (Fig.2). Resulted in comparable Jc enhancement factors (1.5-2×) on both single-crystal and polycrystalline substrates.

tuning_strategies: Utilization of lattice mismatch-induced strain between YBCO (a=3.85Å) and BaZrO₃ (a=4.23Å)
tuning_effects: Generated compressive stress fields around nanoparticles (9.4% mismatch) that created dislocation networks while maintaining Tc >87K. Enabled Jc retention up to 7T through optimized stress relaxation mechanisms without film cracking.
